why: Paragraph 173 has the lad say that three of the sheep have gone lame.
The lad says 'of late' in paragraph 173, so the time point is stated in the story.
Holmes has just asked about anything amiss with the sheep, and the lameness invites the question. The wording does not point to an answer.

text: What lamed the sheep? — an epidemic or chance
why: Disease or chance are ordinary, general explanations for lameness in livestock. The story gives no specific answer, so this is a plain possibility a reader can consider.

text: What lamed the sheep? — someone practised on them
why: The story has already shown someone drugging the stable-boy's supper and Holmes exposing Brown's manipulation of the horse, so deliberate interference with animals is a possibility a reader has reason to consider.
